tips.title: Choosing the Right Knife for Scale Modeling
tips.text: Use a flathead razor blade or a scalpel with a sharp, flat edge for scoring and cutting small plastic or resin parts. The thin, flexible blade allows for precise control and minimizes the risk of damaging surrounding details.

tips.title: Sawing Techniques for Scale Models
tips.text: For cutting metal or thick plastic, use a jeweler's saw or a fine-toothed hobby saw with a fresh blade. Apply gentle, consistent pressure and saw in a smooth, back-and-forth motion, using a sawing motion that is perpendicular to the cutting edge.

tips.title: Files and Their Applications
tips.text: Use a flat file for deburring and smoothing large areas, and a round file for radiusing edges and corners. For more precise work, use a half-round file for curved surfaces or a flat file with a fine tooth for detailed work on small parts.

tips.title: Precision Sanding for Scale Models
tips.text: For fine polishing, use a 240-320 grit wet/dry sandpaper or a 1200-1500 grit polishing paper. Apply a small amount of water or polishing compound to the sandpaper and work in a circular motion, using gentle pressure to avoid scratching the surface.

tips.title: Tool Maintenance and Blade Sharpening
tips.text: To maintain a sharp blade on a hobby saw or jeweler's saw, use a diamond stone or a water stone with a fine grit (e.g., 6000-12000) to sharpen the blade to a 20-30° angle. For flathead razors or scalpels, use a ceramic hone or a leather strop to maintain a sharp, straight edge.
